title: The Agency Capacity Calculator: How Many Clients You Can Run Before Delivery Breaks
subtitle: For 10-50 person agencies: plug in your team, hours, and handoff overhead. Get your real client ceiling, your manual-gap cost, and how many slots automation buys back.

inputs.label: Delivery team size
inputs.hint: Full-time delivery only. Exclude owner, sales, admin.

inputs.label: Productive hours per person per week
inputs.hint: After meetings, breaks, internal admin. Realistic range is 25-32. If you typed 40, you're wrong.

inputs.label: Delivery hours per client per month
inputs.hint: Actual delivery work only. No sales calls, no QBRs.

inputs.label: Manual handoff overhead per client per month
inputs.hint: Time moving info between intake, scoping, delivery, reporting, invoicing. Most agencies underestimate by 2-3x. Never measured? Start at 4.

inputs.label: Fully-loaded cost per delivery hour
inputs.hint: Salary + benefits + overhead divided by billable hours. Typical: $65-$120 for $1M-$10M agencies.

inputs.label: Handoff work currently automated end-to-end
inputs.hint: Most agencies sit between 5% and 20% even when they think they're 'fully on ClickUp.'

recommendations.text: You're already past the line. Delivery quality is what cracks first. Three moves, in order: pause new-business outreach for 30 days, raise prices on the bottom quartile to shed accounts, fix the handoff layer. The math doesn't bend, no matter how many account managers you add.

You're covering the gap with overtime and goodwill. That works until someone senior burns out or a deliverable gets missed. Map your intake → scoping → delivery → reporting handoffs this week. The one with the most human touches is where the next break happens.

One big retainer lands and you're back here doing the same math at 2am. Audit handoff overhead this month, not next quarter. Start with intake — it's the cheapest to fix and the data quality downstream depends on it.

You've got actual room. Lock in handoff automation before sales fills the slots and you're back at the ceiling in 6 months. The window to build the system is when you have time to build it, not when you need it.

You're spending over $10k/month for humans to move information between systems. That's a fully-loaded mid-level hire bleeding out the side of the business every month. Cheapest fix is almost always intake — form data flowing into your PM tool, CRM, and engagement dashboard without a person retyping anything.

Getting your handoff automation to 80% buys you the same hours as hiring another delivery person, at roughly a quarter of the annual cost to maintain. The hiring instinct here is the expensive one. Fix the four handoff points before you write another offer letter.

35+ productive hours per person per week is almost never real once you back out meetings, internal admin, and context-switching. Re-run with 28 and see what your actual ceiling looks like. The number you're publishing is the one your team will quietly miss.
